subject: Model matchmaking post-call: recommended models, parity thresholds and next steps
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <claire@ledgerly.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Ledgerly Procurement <procurement@ledgerly.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo / follow-up: parity checks and next steps

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team liked the latency profile and the KV-caching example. A few asks we discussed that I'd like help turning into concrete next steps:

- Can you recommend a short list (2–3) of open models we should test vs our proprietary baseline for our document-summary + contract-classification flow?
- We want an objective acceptance threshold so we can sign off automatically if the open model meets parity. What do you suggest?
- Can you share the prompt bundles and a small evaluation harness so our SREs can run a quick smoke test?
- Any known quality regression risks (hallucination on legal names, date extraction errors)?

We'd like to get a 2-week eval sprint started next week if possible. Please send a quick plan and any links/attachments we can hand to our engineers.

Best,
Claire
Head of Product, Ledgerly

Attachments: Ledgerly_postcall_notes.pdf (uploaded)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodai.com>
To: Claire Zhou <claire@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo / follow-up: parity checks and next steps

Claire — thanks for the clear ask, really helpful. Quick recap and proposal below.

Recommended short list (to test in week 1):
- OpenCandidate-A (7B, quantized, strong instruction tuning on summarization)
- OpenCandidate-B (13B, better factuality in our internal benchmarks)
- Redwood-Reduced (proprietary baseline variant you already run; used as control)

Proposed acceptance thresholds (initial recommendation):
- Intent / Classification accuracy >= 92% (macro average over contract types)
- Key-extraction F1 >= 90% (names, dates, monetary amounts)
- Hallucination rate < 2% (measured as extraneous facts in ground-truth spans)
- Latency: p95 per-request <= 350ms in your staging profile

Deliverables we’ll share by EOD Monday: prompt bundles (small/medium prompting), a 1000-sample seed evaluation set, and a lightweight harness + instructions to run on your infra. I attached the quick plan (open-vs-prop-benchmark-plan.xlsx) and the prompt JSONL bundle (ledgerly-prompt-sets-v1.jsonl).

Known risks / mitigations:
- Name normalization: OpenCandidate-A sometimes drops honorifics; we’ll include a normalization pipeline in the harness.
- Date formats: ambiguous dates (e.g., 04/05) can flip — we’ll include locale-aware normalization and example prompts that force ISO output.
- Cost / throughput: 13B model has higher token cost; suggest using OpenCandidate-A for initial smoke testing.

Next steps I propose:
1) Your SRE kicks off the harness on Monday using the attached prompt-set; we’ll be on call for the first run.
2) Mid-sprint readout (Friday) with preliminary metrics and any prompt tweaks.
3) Final parity decision meeting at end of week 2.

If that timeline works, I’ll book the readout and loop in our bench team.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ledgerly-prompt-sets-v1.jsonl, open-vs-prop-benchmark-plan.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model matchmaking post-call: recommended models, parity thresholds and next steps

Adding a few specifics for the evaluation sprint and the harness:

- Metric definitions (concrete):
  * Classification accuracy: macro F1 averaged across 8 contract classes.
  * Key-extraction: token-level F1 with span matching using strict start/end.
  * Hallucination: fraction of model output tokens that do not map to any ground-truth span or recognized entity.

- Bench harness: we’ll supply a Docker-based harness and a small runner that supports both hosted API calls (if you want to test Redwood hosted endpoints) and local model invocations. The Drive folder has a README with run commands: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Model-Eval-Playbook

- Prompt bundles: we included 3 temperature variants and a calibrated system prompt for the contract domain. Please run all three in the smoke and report p95 latency and token cost.

- Quality regression guardrails: if hallucination > 2.5% or key-extraction F1 drops by more than 3 points vs baseline, we’ll flag a regression and recommend prompt engineering + light calibration (few-shot examples).

- Quick note on comparability: to be fair, we’ll run the proprietary baseline under the same context window and tokenization; please confirm your preprocessing is identical (esp. date normalization).

Irene — I suggest we attach the HubSpot deal id to the harness run so results auto-post to the deal record.

-Marissa
Senior Research Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodai.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model matchmaking post-call: recommended models, parity thresholds and next steps

Two operational cautions from infra and a small ask for the client:

1) Data handling & PII: ensure the 1k seed eval set is redacted for any live PII. If Ledgerly wants to run on realistic data, we recommend doing that in their VPC / private deployment with our bench runner in network-isolated mode.

2) Canary + fallback: if OpenCandidate-B hits the latency SLO but shows higher hallucinations, we should default to Redwood-Reduced via smart routing for production traffic. We can smoke-test that failover path during the sprint.

3) Ask for Ledgerly: can procurement confirm whether the eval run will be done under a mutual NDA? We can provide a temporary evaluation license if needed.

Irene / Marissa — I’ll be available for the Friday readout.

-Jonas
Director, Platform Partnerships
From: Claire Zhou <claire@ledgerly.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Ledgerly Procurement <procurement@ledgerly.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model matchmaking post-call: recommended models, parity thresholds and next steps

Thanks — this all looks good. Procurement confirms an evaluation NDA (signed yesterday) and they uploaded the redacted 1k sample set to the shared Drive. We’ll kick off the harness Monday morning and aim for the Friday readout.

Two quick clarifications before we start:
- For the hallucination metric, can you include an example rubric so our QA understands what counts as an extraneous fact?
- For key extraction, we’ll want the output in JSON schema (name/date/amount) — is that included in the prompt bundle?

Irene: please go ahead and schedule the Friday 9am PT readout and drop the Drive runbook link in the calendar invite.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Claire
--- End of thread ---
